summary.summary: Customer Hamza Bennani (born 1988, Moroccan national, import-export, medium risk) made three cash deposits on 2026-10-01, 10-03 and 10-05 of 9,400, 9,700 and 9,100 USD, totalling 28,200 USD [E3]. On 2026-10-06 he sent a 27,500 USD wire to 'Mahan Air Co' in Iran [E2]. The counterparty name resembles OFAC SDN entry 'MAHAN AIR' (OFAC:12927), with a name score of 100 [E1]. The deposits and the wire together show a pass-through pattern [E4]. The critical sanctions evidence requires escalation.
rationale: The counterparty on outgoing wire T4 resembles OFAC SDN entry 'MAHAN AIR' (programs SDGT, NPWMD, IFSR) with a name score of 100/100. This is critical severity and mandates escalation. The match is on name only. The list entry has no DOB or nationality to compare, so it needs human confirmation [E1].
The 27,500 USD wire (T4) went to a counterparty in Iran, which is flagged as a high-risk country [E2].
Three cash deposits (T1-T3) each fell just under the 10,000 reporting threshold within 7 days, totalling 28,200 USD. This is consistent with structuring [E3].
Funds left quickly after the last deposits. 27,500 USD was wired out within days of the cash deposits (T2 to T4 within 3 days), which indicates pass-through activity [E4].

The structured cash and the quick onward wire to a counterparty resembling a sanctions list entry are linked by the same transactions (T4 with T1-T3). This raises concern beyond each indicator alone [E1][E3][E4].
